subject.title: [Bug]: Secret provider crash-loop exhausts 1Password service account rate limits

question: What startup SecretRef failure policy should OpenClaw own for side-effecting exec secret providers under launchd/systemd restarts?
rationale: Current behavior intentionally fails fast for active SecretRefs, but retry, degraded startup, circuit breaking, rate-limit handling, and batching each change credential-safety, availability, and operator expectations.

options.title: Generic bounded startup protection
options.body: Add a core-owned, provider-agnostic startup retry/backoff or supervisor-storm mitigation for active SecretRef resolution, with tests and docs that avoid 1Password-specific policy in core.

options.title: Document external resolver caching only
options.body: Keep runtime fail-fast semantics and steer users to Varlock or a custom batched/caching exec resolver plus supervisor restart guidance.

options.title: Adopt provider-specific handling
options.body: Special-case 1Password errors or `op` invocation behavior in core, accepting tighter coupling to a third-party credential tool.

recommendation.title: Generic bounded startup protection
recommendation.body: Add a core-owned, provider-agnostic startup retry/backoff or supervisor-storm mitigation for active SecretRef resolution, with tests and docs that avoid 1Password-specific policy in core.

likelyOwner.reason: The central resolver/runtime SecretRef behavior appears to originate from joshavant's provider-based external secrets and eager snapshot work.
